about: Coach-facing wording Christian has APPROVED for parts of a game the renderer otherwise cannot say: primary-event conditions (register V4-V6) and information rules (V16-V22), and later the modifier criterion and termination (V8c, V8d). His order of 14 October 2026, Step 4 component 3: 'Enable accurate coach-facing communication of scoring conditions and information rules, using approved language.' An entry is used only when it carries approvedBy with who, a date, his words verbatim and the communication standard it was reviewed under; the loader ignores any other entry and a data test fails it. Wording is data, so no sport term enters universal code. Starts EMPTY on 14 October 2026: until he approves a sentence, every such field is withheld and the activity is refused at communication rather than paraphrased. The first entry, A01-W1, was added 18 October 2026 (stage M5): his own sentence for the build-out scoring rule, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1.

entries.sentence: Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score.

approvedBy.quote:
1. Build-out scoring condition — Approved with revised wording
I'd like to simplify the coach-facing wording while preserving the four conditions established in the knowledge.
Suggested wording:
"Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score."
A longer pass received under control remains a valid solution.
The important distinction is that the building team's scoring opportunity applies only during an active build-out episode.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: his own revision of our draft condition sentence, section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 ("The wording that needs your approval"), which put every sentence to him as a draft

entries.note: Added 18 October 2026 (stage M5, design step L13); his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1. One sentence for the build-out scoring rule, said once: the building role's credit bound (B8 = BUILD_OUT_EPISODE, his item 1 and item 3 C, A01-R1-B8-1) and the four conditions his item 1 preserves (origin RPC-001-18.a, progression 18.c, control 18.f, exclusion 19.a), each covered with its exact scope (V3). The match values are the game's own, copied from A01 as the checked pathway builds it at 12 and 11 players, identical in both blocks (measured). The 18.a asAuthored text is the wording he approved on 18 October 2026, item 4 ("I acknowledge and approve your proposed wording": our proposal, approved by him, so not an unapproved gloss of ours), which names both arms of the origin (the goalkeeper, or a controlled defensive restart). His 19 October sentence names only the goalkeeper. OUR INFERRED READING: he narrowed his own wording to the one arm this realization builds, after section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 told him that every build-out in this activity starts with the goalkeeper and the engine cannot yet build the controlled-defensive-restart arm; a test pins that no episode starter of A01 carries a restart kind, so the arm his sentence leaves unnamed cannot occur. The suffixes after ' - ' on the 18.c, 18.f and 19.a asAuthored texts are our glosses, matched here as data only. If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching, the fields are withheld again and A01 is refused at communication (a safe failure).

approvedTemplateSentences.renders: A game whose transition keyed on a change of possession continues play, with one objective per team: the first part cites each such transition's play state and selector, the second the objectives' team and the targets' noun (render-concrete-game.ts, 'How it works'). The second part is said only where the two objectives name different teams; targetNoun is the referenced regions' one noun, and 'line' where they name no other.
parts: When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage
, and each team keeps attacking the same {targetNoun}
approvedTemplateSentences.sentence: When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage, and each team keeps attacking the same zone.

approvedBy.quote: I approve both of your proposed revisions: … Use: "When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage, and each team keeps attacking the same zone." For the second sentence, please ensure the surrounding scoring instructions make clear that continuing to attack does not automatically restore the building team's eligibility to score.
